title: A hymn in Bhairao
hookLine: Namdev carries a cup of milk to the Lord, and Guru Arjan names the One he serves

lines: A BROWN COW AND A CUP.
HE CARRIES IT TO THE LORD.
cards: A brown cow, a pail, and someone who has been given a job. He milks the cow, pours the milk into a cup, fills a jug with water, and carries both to the Lord. Then he waits for the Lord to drink.

That's the opening of a hymn by Bhagat Namdev, in his own words, in the Bhairao section of the Guru Granth Sahib. You may remember this cup from Namdev's week in year three. Today it gets a second, slower look.

teach.h: MILK IN A CUP, WATER IN A JUG.
teach.b: Here's the hymn, in paraphrase. Namdev milks the brown cow and brings the milk in a cup, with water in a jug.

teach.h: DRINK, AND MY MIND WILL BE AT PEACE.
teach.b: He sets it before the Lord and pleads: drink this, Lord, and my mind will be at peace. If you don't, my father at home will be angry. Then the turn.
A golden cup, filled with nectar, is set before the Lord, and the hymn has God say that this one devotee lives in his heart, and smile on seeing Namdev.

The Lord drinks the milk. The devotee goes home, and Namdev has seen the Lord. Tradition fills in the edges: Namdev was a child, and his father, who usually made the daily offering, had asked him to do it.
The hymn itself keeps it simple: a cup, a plea, a smile, an empty cup. What stays with people is his directness. He doesn't offer the milk as a ritual to perform and clear away.
He offers it as a gift to someone really there, and he means it to be received.
The same section holds a hymn of Guru Arjan about serving only the One who protects in the end, which says body and breath belong to the One called both Allah and Ram.
Two voices, one point: devotion is offered to someone present.

And looking back over this week, from Maru's true warrior through Tukhari's months, Kedara's tender evening and Bhairao's serious morning, each raga has handed over something to carry. Today it's a cup.

how: Namdev's hymns in the Guru Granth Sahib are sung in kirtan alongside the Gurus' own, and the milk hymn in Bhairao is retold with the story of the boy Namdev making the offering.

in the hymn, the Lord drinks the milk
the Lord smiles on seeing Namdev, drinks, and Namdev goes home having seen the Lord.

games.q: you're Namdev. you've set the milk before the Lord and nothing happens. what do you do?
o: pour it out and go home.
plead with the Lord to drink it.
drink it yourself so no one knows.
games.why: in the hymn Namdev pleads: drink, and my mind will be at peace. the Lord smiles and drinks.

practice: Bring to mind one ordinary thing you'll give today, a meal you'll cook, a message you'll answer, an hour of work, and hold it the way Namdev holds the cup: not a chore to clear, but something meant to be received.
Breathe slowly around it. If you pray, offer it with Waheguru on the breath; if you don't, simply let the giving be wholehearted.

wordCard.voice: A hymn in Bhairao. Namdev's song of the cup of milk he carries to the Lord, pleading for it to be drunk, and the Lord smiling and drinking. Today's word.

orig.note: milk: the hymn opens with milk in a cup and water in a jug.

carryVoice: Your line: the milk offering. Namdev's cup was a gift to someone present, never a chore. That's today, done.
